Yes, and for **your environment**, I think `.prompt.md` files may become even more valuable than Skills in some cases.

The key is understanding the difference:

|Feature|Purpose|Automatic?|Best For|
|---|---|---|---|
|`copilot-instructions.md`|Global rules and conventions|✅ Yes|Coding standards|
|`SKILL.md`|Specialized expertise/workflows|✅ When relevant|FME, CYME, Jira knowledge|
|`*.prompt.md`|Reusable commands/tasks|❌ Invoked manually|Frequent activities|
|Agents|Persona + tools|Depends|Architect, Reviewer, BA|

GitHub describes Prompt Files as **reusable prompts for common tasks** that you invoke when needed, typically through a `/command` in chat. [[docs.github.com]](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/tutorials/customization-library/prompt-files), [[docs.github.com]](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/tutorials/customization-library/prompt-files/your-first-prompt-file), [[copilot-ac....github.io]](https://copilot-academy.github.io/workshops/copilot-customization/copilot_customization_handbook)

---

# What is a `.prompt.md`?

Suppose you frequently ask Copilot:

> Create a Jira ticket following our team's template.

Instead of rewriting that request every time, you create:

.github/prompts/create-jira.prompt.md

Example:

---  

description: Create a Jira ticket using CYME standards  

agent: agent  

---  

  

Create a Jira ticket using the following format:  

  

Title:  

- concise and action-oriented  

  

Description:  

- Background  

- Changes  

- Acceptance Criteria  

  

Use the selected text as the source material:  

  

${selection}

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Then, in Copilot Chat, you simply type:

/create-jira

and it executes the predefined workflow. [[docs.github.com]](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/tutorials/customization-library/prompt-files/your-first-prompt-file), [[github.com]](https://github.com/fadwen/Powershell-Copilot-Standards/blob/main/Documentation/Prompt-Files-Guide.md)

# Prompt Files vs Skills

For your use case:

### Skill

fme-expert  

contains:

- FME knowledge
- transformer recommendations
- company conventions

It teaches Copilot **how to think**.

---

### Prompt File

analyze-fme.prompt.md

contains:

- specific task
- expected output
- report format

It tells Copilot **what to do**.

Think:

Skill = expertise  

  

Prompt = command

---

# Will it improve results?

**Absolutely, if your requests are repetitive.**

Instead of:

Create a Jira ticket.  

Use our format.  

Create acceptance criteria.  

Use a technical writing style.

every time...

you write:

/create-jira  

``

The result is:

- more consistency
- less typing
- better standardization
- easier onboarding for your team
- fewer "forgotten instructions" by Copilot

### English correction

> "I have learned a few days ago that Github Copilot uses a file named `name.prompt.md`."

More natural:

> **"I learned a few days ago that GitHub Copilot supports files named `*.prompt.md`. What are they, and should I use them?"**

Notes:

- "I learned" sounds more natural here than "I have learned".
- Use **GitHub** (capital H).
- `*.prompt.md` better represents the pattern than `name.prompt.md`.
